{"items":[{"content":{"body":"# Stage S1 — Control-plane validation

Validates the Gatebraid Classic control plane end to end on the scratch
repository: the Stage/Phase/Slice hierarchy, the two dependency encodings of
ADR-0007, and the Project field contract of spec §1–§3. This Stage delivers
evidence that the control plane behaves as specified before any business work
is admitted to it.

## Scope

- A four-Slice sample hierarchy carrying both dependency encodings.
- A read-only verification pass proving metadata and native edges agree with
  ADR-0007.

## Phases

<!-- Maintained as sub-issues; list here is informational and may lag. -->
- P1 — Sample hierarchy and dependency encoding (sub-issue)


Builds the four-Slice sample hierarchy in the scratch repository and encodes
the two ADR-0007 dependency forms across it: metadata-only edges for Gate 1
and Gate 2 predecessors, and metadata plus a native blocked-by edge for the
single Gate 3 predecessor. The Phase exists so the soft and hard encodings can
be observed diverging on the same graph.

## Slices

<!-- Maintained as sub-issues; list here is informational and may lag. -->
- P1-S1 — Define the shared interface (sub-issue, in MianliWang/gatebraid-scratch)
- P1-S2 — Build on the interface A fixes at Gate 1 (sub-issue, in MianliWang/gatebraid-scratch)
- P1-S3 — Consume A's released output (sub-issue, in MianliWang/gatebraid-scratch)
- P1-S4 — Integrate B and C (sub-issue, in MianliWang/gatebraid-scratch)
- P1-S5 — Consume A's released output (sub-issue, in MianliWang/gatebraid-scratch) — successor to the aborted P1-S3

","number":3,"repository":"MianliWang/gatebraid","title":"Phase P1 — Sample hierarchy and dependency encoding","type":"Issue","url":"https://github.com/MianliWang/gatebraid/issues/3"},"id":"PVTI_lAHOBRofUs4Beum7zg0oahM","phase":"P1","repository":"https://github.com/MianliWang/gatebraid","stage":"S1","status":"Todo","title":"Phase P1 — Sample hierarchy and dependency encoding"},{"active Branch":"slice/P1-S1","base SHA":"1c178e1aff77b54940abad140a934cb555f5662d","content":{"body":"# P1-S1 — gatebraid-snapshot: a read-only dump of the Project's state

## Goal

A single command that dumps the complete state of the "Mianli Engineering"
Project as JSON: fields and their options, views with their filters, grouping,
sorting and visible fields, every item with every field value, the issue
hierarchy, native dependency edges in both directions, and the built-in
workflow list.

Python 3 standard library only, plus authenticated `gh` for transport
(ADR-0009). Read-only by construction.

## Context

- Why now: every verification pass through M1 and M2 hand-wrote these GraphQL
  queries. Turning that into one command makes every later read-back cheaper,
  and — more importantly — consistent, so two runs are comparable.
- Why this slice is first: it has zero write blast radius, which is the right
  risk profile for the first execution of the gate contracts, and it has a
  crisp negative criterion a reviewer can check absolutely.
- Non-goals: **no readiness computation.** This is a snapshot, not a frontier.
  `gatebraid-frontier` is M3's job and this slice must not anticipate it. No
  mutation of any kind. No caching, no diffing, no scheduling.
- Related: Stage S1 `MianliWang/gatebraid#2`, Phase P1 `MianliWang/gatebraid#3`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bin/gatebraid-snapshot.py` exists in this repository and runs on the host
      with Python 3 standard library only. Check: `python3 bin/gatebraid-snapshot.py --help`
- [ ] Running it writes a single JSON document to stdout and nothing else.
      Check: `python3 bin/gatebraid-snapshot.py > /tmp/snap.json && python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('/tmp/snap.json'))"`
- [ ] The document contains, as named top-level keys: `project`, `fields`,
      `views`, `items`, `hierarchy`, `dependencies`, `workflows`.
- [ ] The numbers match the state recorded in the M1 verification manifest:
      **14** custom fields, **12** views, **6** non-archived items, **1**
      archived item, **1** native dependency edge, **6** built-in workflows.
      Check: a small assertion script run against the output, its command and
      output embedded in the Gate 2 evidence.
- [ ] Archived items are only included when explicitly requested, and the
      default excludes them — matching `ProjectV2.items`' own semantics, which
      silently drop archived items unless `archivedStates` is passed.
- [ ] Dependency edges are reported in **both** directions (`blocked_by` and
      `blocking`), because reading one direction alone can miss an edge.

## Negative criterion (checked at Gate 2 review item R4)

**The diff contains no GitHub mutation.** Concretely, nowhere in the added code:
a `gh api` call with `--method` set to anything but `GET`; a `gh issue`,
`gh pr`, `gh project` or `gh label` subcommand that creates, edits, deletes,
closes or merges; or a GraphQL document containing the token `mutation`.

## Out of scope

Anything not required by the acceptance list. If the plan needs to widen,
that is a `Scope / Allowlist Change`, not a judgement call.

Lands `bin/gatebraid-capture.py` and `bin/gatebraid-capture-selftest.py`

through gates 0–3 in the control repository (ADR-0032 decisions 1, 2

Accept-when is dual-platform by construction: every measurement runs on
Windows (CPython 3.12.2, jsonschema 4.23.0) AND WSL Ubuntu 24.04
(CPython 3.12.3, jsonschema 4.10.3), and both must be green — including
the guard-versus-Draft202012Validator cross-check, which is a real

control repository — a configuration no gate contract has been exercised
in. Any contract clause that cannot be satisfied as written in this
configuration is a STOP and a finding under ADR-0032's first reopening
condition, never an improvisation.

`schema/` are outside the allowlist, and any needed change there is an
approved N1 correct-course, not Slice work.

`depends_on` is empty: P2-S1 consumes corpus v1.1 from the base commit
of its own branch, not from any Slice's released output, and the control
repository's issues carry no dependency edges (measured, N2-G0R).

## Goal

Land M3's independent evidence validator: the tool that re-derives verdicts
from captured evidence JSON and the frozen schemas alone, publishes a
`gatebraid/coverage-report@1` classifying every verified property, and kills
the N1 corpus mutations independently of the generator (M3-PLAN §2 N3;
ADR-0031 N3-start freeze; ADR-0032 decisions 1 and 5). The script's official
name is ratified per ADR-0030 in this Slice's State Packet Approval, not
assumed here.

## Context

- Why now: N2 (P2-S1, #8) is landed and closed; the N2/N3 bootstrap boundary
  expires at N2 + N3 Gate 3 completion, and N3 re-validates N2's
  bootstrap-marked records after its own Gate 3.
- Independence: authored without reading N2's implementation — the authoring
  session receives the frozen schemas and the N1 corpus only; the
  imports-and-authorship independence review is performed by the coordinator
  from the record before freeze (M3-PLAN §2 N3).
- Non-goals: no change to any N2 file; no corpus change (IN-01 is
  re-assigned to corpus v2 at P); no O0 material; no contract, schema, ADR
  or template edit.
- Related: Stage S2 `#6` · Phase P2 `#7` · P2-S1 `#8` ·
  `schema/coverage-report.schema.json` · ADR-0028 / ADR-0030 / ADR-0031 /
  ADR-0032.

## Acceptance
